subject: SecureEdge private hosting discovery — summary & action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@secureedge.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SecureEdge private hosting discovery — recap and immediate next steps

Asha — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we all have the same record.

Pain points you called out:
- Data residency & auditability for PII/PHI (SOC2 + HIPAA controls required)
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) and Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration
- Strict egress rules and an isolated VPC with no internet outbound for inference nodes (air-gap to partner APIs)
- Predictable latency for real-time inference (95th %-ile < 150ms per request)

Current stack you mentioned:
- Core app hosted in SecureEdge VPC (AWS us-west-2)
- In-house KMS (HashiCorp Vault) + on-prem HSM for key material
- Kubernetes for app deployment; GPUs in separate, isolated subnet

Success criteria (how you’ll evaluate a solution):
1) No customer data leaves the VPC unless explicitly permitted
2) Redwood-managed control plane with private connectivity to customer VPC (VPC peering / PrivateLink / transit)
3) Support for customer KMS/HSM and per-tenant key rotation
4) SLA on inference latency and availability

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- Redwood to provide a candidate architecture diagram showing Private control plane connectivity options (we’ll attach a network sketch)
- SecureEdge to share a redacted network diagram and a sample compliance checklist (requested by Thu, 11 Nov)
- Schedule a deep-dive workshop with your infra/security team to validate KMS/HSM integration (proposed window: week of Nov 16)
- Draft SOW outline for on-prem/VPC deployment and license model for dedicated nodes

Attachments: network_diagram.pdf (sketch), sow-draft.docx (initial outline)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll aim to send the architecture sketch and SOW outline by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — rishi

--

From: Asha Patel <asha@secureedge.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SecureEdge private hosting discovery — recap and immediate next steps

Thanks Rishi — this looks right, appreciate the clear summary.

Two clarifications:
1) Our compliance lead (cc’d: it@secureedge.ai) will need a data-flow diagram that shows where logs and telemetry land. Can you include expected audit log locations and retention options?
2) For HSM we run a Thales backup appliance on site; we need to confirm Redwood can work with either our on-prem HSM or provide a validated HSM integration path.

We’ll attach a redacted network diagram and a compliance checklist by end of day Thursday. Please hold the week of Nov 16 for the workshop — we’ll confirm a day once I check calendars.

—Asha

On a separate note: can you include a rough cost band for an initial pilot (3 dedicated GPUs, 3 months)? We don’t need exact pricing yet, just a ballpark for planning.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@secureedge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SecureEdge private hosting discovery — recap and immediate next steps

Asha — thanks. A couple of follow-ups from the infra perspective:

- For the audit logs: Redwood Private can be configured to push audit trails to an S3-compatible endpoint in your VPC or to an on-prem object store; we’ll include retention policy templates in the compliance package.
- KMS/HSM: We support Vault-based BYOK flows and have a validated integration pattern for Thales HSMs; will include the integration checklist in the workshop agenda.
- Network options: PrivateLink inside AWS or a short-lived VPN + routing for the control plane; we’ll sketch both in the diagram. For strict no-outbound use-cases we can run an isolated control plane appliance on-prem — that’s heavier but possible.

I attached the network diagram sketch and a very rough SOW outline (placeholders for costs). Please treat the SOW as draft — numbers will change after the workshop.

Attachments: network_diagram.pdf, sow-draft.docx

Thanks,
Monica
